## Objective

- Understand what an IDE is
- Learn IDE features that improve productivity and workflow
- See why VS Code enables agentic workflows

## What is an IDE (Integrated Development Environment)?

* Code is just text and can be edited in any text editor. An IDE is basically a text editor on steroids. 

* Some languages have their own editors with features specifically designed for that language
    * E.g., Stata's do-file editor, RStudio for R.

* IDEs like VS Code are not tied to one programming language, which means they have a much broader user base.

* That large user base constantly develops small productivity and code-management tools, made available through custom extensions and plugins.

## Why use an IDE?

* IDEs with large userbases tend to adopt the latest tools first. Using an IDE with a wide userbase is very helpful for staying up to date with the latest developments

* AI is changing very quickly, and smaller language-specific code editors likely lag behind.

* Switching from a language-specific editor to a general IDE like VS Code may take some time, but the long-term gains in productivity and access to new tools outweigh the initial cost of adoption (J-curve)

* Once you become comfortable with an IDE like VS Code, you will likely feel like a more capable coder and it is likely hard to imagine going back to older workflows. :)
